title: November 2026 Housing Market Brief
headline: New evidence on residential permitting, inflation-adjusted home values, active listings in Orange County, and seller repricing in Orange County
summary: Yes. Los Angeles metro YTD permits rose 37.6%. No. Los Angeles metro home values changed +1.3% from one year earlier, while LA-area CPI-U changed +3.7% over the same period. The implied inflation-adjusted change was -2.4%. Orange County active listings increased by 20.7% from one year earlier. Orange County active listings with price drops increased by 4.3 percentage points; 34 of 41 covered local markets increased.
reconstruction_note: Prepared from the Lab’s validated fact packet. Each finding retains its observation period and source release; later provider revisions do not silently alter this archived edition.

qualification_paths.material_movement: The primary measure crossed its fixed editorial threshold.
qualification_paths.broad_local_shift: At least 65% of covered local markets moved in one direction and the median change reached half of its editorial threshold.
qualification_paths.direction_change: The year-over-year comparison changed sign, with the current and preceding changes each reaching at least half of the editorial threshold.
qualification_paths.indicator_divergence: Two pre-specified related indicators moved in meaningfully different directions or separated by a pre-specified gap.

sections.question: Is residential permitting increasing?
sections.answer: Yes. Los Angeles metro YTD permits rose 37.6%.
evidence: Los Angeles metro: 26,937 units authorized YTD vs. 19,572 in the same months last year.
sections.sources: U.S. Census Bureau Building Permits Survey
sections.coverage: Matched permit jurisdictions in Los Angeles and Orange counties; sum of county counts, not an official BPS metro series
sections.caveat: Current-year observations are preliminary and may be revised or imputed; permits are authorizations, not starts or completions.

sections.question: Are home values keeping pace with local inflation?
sections.answer: No. Los Angeles metro home values changed +1.3% from one year earlier, while LA-area CPI-U changed +3.7% over the same period. The implied inflation-adjusted change was -2.4%.
evidence: Nominal ZHVI changed +1.3% while LA-area CPI-U changed +3.7%.
sections.sources: Zillow Research + U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics
sections.coverage: Common-month Zillow ZHVI and LA-area CPI-U
sections.caveat: Real change is a purchasing-power comparison, not an affordability measure. Not seasonally adjusted; the area index covers Los Angeles and Orange Counties. The latest index observation (2026-10-31) has no calculable year-over-year change; this comparison uses 2026-09-30.

sections.question: Is active inventory changing broadly across Orange County?
sections.answer: Orange County active listings increased by 20.7% from one year earlier.
evidence: Orange County: The median local change was +20.7%; among 57 markets with calculable changes, 38 increased, 18 decreased, and 1 was unchanged.
sections.coverage: 57 of 85 local markets had calculable year-over-year changes
sections.caveat: Unweighted median across covered local markets; it is not a county aggregate.

evidence: Orange County: The median local change was +4.3 percentage points; among 41 markets with calculable changes, 34 increased, 7 decreased, and 0 were unchanged.
sections.coverage: 41 of 42 local markets had calculable year-over-year changes
sections.caveat: Unweighted median across covered cities using Redfin rolling three-month estimates; it is not a county aggregate.
